q: The Hopf invariant of a map f: S³ → S² classifies elements of π₃(S²). The Hopf fibration η: S³ → S² has Hopf invariant:
exp: The Hopf fibration η: S³ → S² (fibers are great circles S¹) has Hopf invariant 1, generating π₃(S²) ≅ ℤ. The Hopf invariant-1 problem (Adams, 1960) showed the only maps with Hopf invariant 1 occur in dimensions 1, 2, 4, 8 (related to division algebras).
